{{Short description|French cosmologist (born 1969)}}
[[File:Jean-Philippe Uzan - Utopiales 2015 - E96A0733.JPG|thumb|Image of Jean-Philippe Uzan ]]
'''Jean-Philippe Uzan''' (born 1969) is a French cosmologist and ''[[Academic ranks in France#Research-only positions|directeur de recherche]]'' employed by the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS).

==Education and career==
In 1987 Uzan graduated from secondary school with the degree ''Baccalauréat C'' with honours. From 1987 to 1990 he studied at [[Lycée Saint-Louis]] to prepare for competitive scientific examinations. From 1990 to 1993 he studied in the Engineering School of the [[Mines Paris - PSL|École des Mines de Paris]]. There he graduated in 1993 with a civil engineering degree with specialisation in Earth science. From 1993 to 1994 he did his French military service as a cooperant doing research at the ''Institutet for rymdfysik'' (IRF, [[Swedish Institute of Space Physics]]). At [[Paris-Sud University]] (Paris XI), he obtained a [[Master of Advanced Studies|''Diplôme d'études approfondies'' (DEA)]] in [[theoretical physics]] and then completed a Ph.D. [[thesis]] in theoretical physics in 1998.<ref name=IAP>{{cite web|title=Jean-Philippe Uzan (CNRS)|website=Institut d'Astrophysique de Paris|url=http://www2.iap.fr/users/uzan/}}</ref> His thesis was supervised by [[Nathalie Deruelle]],<ref>{{cite thesis|lang=fr|author=Uzan, Jean-Philippe |title=Défauts topologiques et conditions aux limites en cosmologie primordiale |website=Thèse de doctorat |publisher=Paris 11 |year=1998 |url=http://www.theses.fr/1998PA112143 |type=These de doctorat }}</ref> who worked at the (DARC, Department of Relativistic Astrophysics and Cosmology) at the [[Meudon Observatory]]. After holding a postdoctoral position under the supervision of [[:en:Ruth Durrer|Ruth Durrer]] at the department of theoretical physics of the [[University of Geneva]], he was recruited in 1999 at the CNRS (section 02) and assigned to the physics laboratory theory from the [[University of Paris-Sud]] (Paris XI) at [[Orsay]]. He was assigned in 2005 to the [[Institut d'Astrophysique de Paris]] (IAP) and appointed ''directeur de recherche'' in 2009. He received his [[habilitation]] degree (''Habilitation à diriger des recherches'', HDR) in 2007 from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris 6).<ref name=IAP/>

Uzan specializes in gravitation and relativistic cosmology and is the author or coauthor of more than 130 articles in peer-reviewed journals.<ref name=IAP/> He is an editor for the journal ''[[Foundations of Physics]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Editors|website=Foundations of Physics|publisher=Springer|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/10701/editors}}</ref>

From June 2013 to June 2017 he was the deputy director, with [[Cédric Villani]] as director, of the [[Institut Henri-Poincaré]] (IHP). Uzan contributed to the expansion of the institute and the creation of the Maison des Mathématiques containing, among other things, a museum of mathematics.<ref>{{cite web|title=La Maison des mathématiques 2020, Chapitre 1|publisher=Institut Henri Poincaré|date=June 14, 2017|website=YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AFLhIUGdBLE}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=La Maison des mathématiques 2020, Chapitre 2|publisher=Institut Henri Poincaré|date=December 22, 2017|website=YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=79obSq24tyw}}</ref> He co-authored, with Cédric Villani and Vincent Moncorgé, the book ''La Maison des Mathématiques'' (2015) describing the life of the institute. Uzan also directed the collective work ''Modèles mathématiques'' (2017), describing the collection of models from the IHP library. In 2015, for the 100th anniversary of the publication of Einstein's theory of general relativity, Uzan co-authored and presented the documentary ''Einstein et la Relativité Générale, une histoire singulière'' (Einstein and General Relativity, a unique story). Directed by filmmaker Quentin Lazzarotto, the film features major international researchers such as [[Jocelyn Bell Burnell]], [[Roger Penrose]], [[Thibault Damour]], and [[Carlo Rovelli]].<ref>{{cite web |language=fr |title=Einstein et la Relativité Générale |url=https://www.nebuleuseprod.com/einstein |website=Nébuleuse Productions |date=19 February 2016 }}</ref>

Uzan was one of the keynote speakers invited for the public session of the 26th meeting of the ''Conférence générale des poids et mesures'' (CGPM, [[General Conference on Weights and Measures]]) on the day of the vote on the historical revision of the [[International System of Units]] on November 16, 2018, in Versailles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jean-Philippe Uzan - "The role of the Planck constant in physics" 26th CGPM|publisher=The BIPM|website=YouTube|date=November 16, 2018|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yhgb23tAFFs}}</ref>

He has collaborated with many artists and is the author or coauthor of nine popular science books. He also works on [[science outreach]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jean-Philippe Uzan|website=Villa Albertine|url=https://villa-albertine.org/residents/jean-philippe-uzan}}</ref>

==Research==
Jean-Philippe Uzan is a specialist in gravitation and relativistic cosmology. He worked on several aspects related to [[observational cosmology]] and the cosmology of the [[early universe]].

He has developed numerous tests of [[general relativity]] at astrophysical and cosmological scales. The study of [[fundamental constants]]<ref>{{cite journal | last=Uzan | first=Jean-Philippe | title=The fundamental constants and their variation: observational and theoretical status | journal=Reviews of Modern Physics | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=75 | issue=2 | date=2003-04-07 | issn=0034-6861 | doi=10.1103/revmodphys.75.403 | pages=403–455| arxiv=hep-ph/0205340 | bibcode=2003RvMP...75..403U | s2cid=118684485 |url=http://rmp.aps.org/abstract/RMP/v75/i2/p403_1/}}</ref> offers a test of the [[equivalence principle]] at the heart of Einstein's theory of gravitation. He established several constraints on fundamental constants' possible variations, in particular, from [[primordial nucleosynthesis]],<ref>{{cite journal|title = Coupled variations of fundamental couplings and primordial nucleosynthesis | author = Coc, Alain |author2= Nunes, Nelson J. |author3=Olive, Keith A.|author4=Uzan, Jean-Philippe |author5=Vangioni, Elisabeth | journal = Physical Review D | volume = 76 | issue=2 |pages = 023511–023522 |date=July 2007 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevD.76.023511 | arxiv = astro-ph/0610733 | bibcode = 2007PhRvD..76b3511C | s2cid = 30230380 | url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.76.023511}}</ref> [[cosmic microwave background]],<ref>{{cite journal| title=Planck intermediate results. XXIV. D. | arxiv=1406.7482 | bibcode=2015A&A...580A..22P | s2cid=33250997 | display-authors=1 }} [https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.7482 arXiv preprint]</ref> [[Stellar population#Population III stars|population III stars]],<ref>{{cite conference | last1=Coc | first1=A. | last2=Ekström | first2=S. | last3=Descouvemont | first3=P. | last4=Meynet | first4=G. | last5=Uzan | first5=J.-Ph. | last6=Vangioni | first6=E. | last7=Tanihara | first7=Isao | last8=Ong | first8=Hooi Jin | last9=Tamii | first9=Atsushi | last10=Kishimoto | first10=Tadafumi | last11=Kajino | first11=Toshitaka | last12=Kubono | first12=Shigeru | last13=Shima | first13=Tatsushi | title=Effects of the variation of fundamental constants on Pop III stellar evolution | series=AIP Conference Proceedings | publisher=AIP | year=2010 | pages=21–26 | issn=0094-243X | doi=10.1063/1.3485139 | arxiv=0911.2420 }} [https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.2420 arXiv preprint]</ref> and the [[MICROSCOPE (satellite)|MICROSCOPE satellite results]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.141101 |title=MICROSCOPE Mission: First Constraints on the Violation of the Weak Equivalence Principle by a Light Scalar Dilaton |year=2018 |last1=Bergé |first1=Joel |last2=Brax |first2=Philippe |last3=Métris |first3=Gilles |last4=Pernot-Borràs |first4=Martin |last5=Touboul |first5=Pierre |last6=Uzan |first6=Jean-Philippe |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=120 |issue=14 |article-number=141101 |pmid=29694146 |arxiv=1712.00483 |bibcode=2018PhRvL.120n1101B |s2cid=206309271 |url=https://hal-cea.archives-ouvertes.fr/cea-01686662v2/file/BeBrPeTo.pdf }}</ref> He studied tensor-scalar theories (such as [[tensor–vector–scalar gravity]], [[scalar–tensor–vector gravity]] and [[bi-scalar tensor vector gravity]]), various potential alternatives to general relativity, and their observational signatures in cosmology (primordial nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, and [[Observable universe#Large-scale structure|large-scale structure]]). In 2001, he proposed, with Francis Bernardeau of the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission|Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives (CEA)]], a test<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.64.083004 |title=Lensing at cosmological scales: A test of higher dimensional gravity |year=2001 |last1=Uzan |first1=Jean-Philippe |last2=Bernardeau |first2=Francis |journal=Physical Review D |volume=64 |issue=8 |article-number=083004 |arxiv=hep-ph/0012011 |bibcode=2001PhRvD..64h3004U |s2cid=119455304 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/s10714-006-0385-z |title=The acceleration of the universe and the physics behind it |year=2007 |last1=Uzan |first1=Jean-Philippe |journal=[[General Relativity and Gravitation]] |volume=39 |issue=3 |pages=307–342 |arxiv=astro-ph/0605313 |s2cid=118989708 }}</ref> of general relativity at cosmological scales.

In observational cosmology, he has worked on primordial nucleosynthesis, the cosmic microwave background, [[Observable Universe#Large-scale structure|large-scale structure]], the effects of gravitational lensing and the diffuse background of gravitational waves.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Cusin | first1=Giulia | last2=Pitrou | first2=Cyril | last3=Uzan | first3=Jean-Philippe | title=Anisotropy of the astrophysical gravitational wave background: Analytic expression of the angular power spectrum and correlation with cosmological observations | journal=Physical Review D | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=96 | issue=10 | date=2017-11-28 | article-number=103019 | issn=2470-0010 | doi=10.1103/physrevd.96.103019| arxiv=1704.06184 | bibcode=2017PhRvD..96j3019C | s2cid=118967586 }} [https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.06184 arXiv preprint]</ref> In particular, he obtained the first prediction of the power spectrum of the stochastic background of gravitational waves of astrophysical origin and the power spectrum's correlations with the distribution of galaxies and the effects of gravitational shear.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cusin |first1=Giulia |last2=Dvorkin |first2=Irina |last3=Pitrou |first3=Cyril |last4=Uzan |first4=Jean-Philippe |year=2018 |title=First Predictions of the Angular Power Spectrum of the Astrophysical Gravitational Wave Background |url=https://hal.science/hal-01757978/file/PhysRevLett.120.231101.pdf |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=120 |issue=23 |article-number=231101 |arxiv=1803.03236 |bibcode=2018PhRvL.120w1101C |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.231101 |pmid=29932710 |s2cid=49379620}} [https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03236]. See also the CNRS journal article: {{cite journal |author=Ter Minassian, Vahé |date=2018-06-19 |title=Décrypter la rumeur des cataclysmes cosmiques |url=https://lejournal.cnrs.fr/articles/decrypter-la-rumeur-des-cataclysmes-cosmiques |journal=Le Journal |publisher=CNRS}}</ref> With Julien Larena and Pierre Fleury, he proposed in 2015 "stochastic lensing", a new approach to the effects of small-scale structures on the effects of gravitational lensing in cosmology<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fleury |first1=Pierre |last2=Larena |first2=Julien |last3=Uzan |first3=Jean-Philippe |year=2015 |title=The theory of stochastic cosmological lensing |journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics |volume=2015 |issue=11 |page=022 |arxiv=1508.07903 |bibcode=2015JCAP...11..022F |doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2015/11/022 |s2cid=118389041}} [https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.07903]</ref> and in 2017 a solution to the Ricci-Weyl problem.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.191101 |title=Weak Gravitational Lensing of Finite Beams |year=2017 |last1=Fleury |first1=Pierre |last2=Larena |first2=Julien |last3=Uzan |first3=Jean-Philippe |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=119 |issue=19 |article-number=191101 |pmid=29219481 |arxiv=1706.09383 |bibcode=2017PhRvL.119s1101F |s2cid=206302118 |url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-01645589/file/fleury2017.pdf }}</ref>

He proposed various tests of the assumptions on which the [[standard model of cosmology]] is based. See, for an overview, his reviews.
<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1007/s10714-010-1047-8 |title=Tests of general relativity on astrophysical scales |year=2010 |last1=Uzan |first1=Jean-Philippe |journal=General Relativity and Gravitation |volume=42 |issue=9 |pages=2219–2246 |arxiv=0908.2243 |bibcode=2010GReGr..42.2219U |s2cid=14667139 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|year=2010|editor=Ruiz-Lapuente, Pilar|chapter=Chapter 1. ''Dark energy, gravitation and the Copernican principle'' by Jean-Philippe Uzan|title=Dark Energy: observational and theoretical approaches|pages=3–47|bibcode=2010deot.book.....R }} [https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.5452 arXiv preprint]</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv | eprint=1606.06112 | last1=Uzan | first1=Jean-Philippe | title=The big-bang theory: Construction, evolution and status | year=2016 | class=astro-ph.CO }}</ref> He proposed in 2008, with [[George F. R. Ellis]] and Chris Clarkson, a test of the Copernican principle<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.100.191303 |title=Time Drift of Cosmological Redshifts as a Test of the Copernican Principle |year=2008 |last1=Uzan |first1=Jean-Philippe |last2=Clarkson |first2=Chris |last3=Ellis |first3=George F. R. |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=100 |issue=19 |article-number=191303 |pmid=18518435 |arxiv=0801.0068 |bibcode=2008PhRvL.100s1303U |s2cid=31455609 |url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-03646439/file/uzan2008-1.pdf }}</ref> and in 2016, with Cyril Pitrou and Thiago Pereira, a test of the isotropy of the expansion of the universe.<ref>{{cite journal| doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201527258 | title=Weak-lensing B-modes as a probe of the isotropy of the universe | year=2016 | last1=Pereira | first1=Thiago S. | last2=Pitrou | first2=Cyril | last3=Uzan | first3=Jean-Philippe | journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics | volume=585 | pages=L3 | arxiv=1503.01127 | bibcode=2016A&A...585L...3P | s2cid=118463946 }}</ref> Uzan with collaborators also proposed several tests of [[Etherington's reciprocity theorem|Etherington's cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR)]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Uzan | first1=Jean-Philippe | last2=Aghanim | first2=Nabila | last3=Mellier | first3=Yannick | title=Distance duality relation from x-ray and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich observationsof clusters | journal=Physical Review D | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=70 | issue=8 | date=2004-10-27 | issn=1550-7998 | doi=10.1103/physrevd.70.083533 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.70.083533 |pages=083533–083539| arxiv=astro-ph/0405620 | bibcode=2004PhRvD..70h3533U | s2cid=119430471 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Ellis, George F. R.|author2=Poltis, Robert|author3= Uzan, J. P.|author4=Weltman, Amanda|author-link4=Amanda Weltman|year=2013|title=Blackness of the cosmic microwave background spectrum as a probe of the distance-duality relation|journal=Physical Review D|volume=87|issue=10|pages=103530–103535|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.87.103530 |arxiv=1301.1312 |bibcode=2013PhRvD..87j3530E |s2cid=118469478 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.87.103530}}</ref> He also studied the [[topology of the universe]] and obtained numerous constraints on the size and shape of the universe.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1038/nature01944 |title=Dodecahedral space topology as an explanation for weak wide-angle temperature correlations in the cosmic microwave background |year=2003 |last1=Luminet |first1=Jean-Pierre |last2=Weeks |first2=Jeffrey R. |last3=Riazuelo |first3=Alain |last4=Lehoucq |first4=Roland |last5=Uzan |first5=Jean-Philippe |journal=Nature |volume=425 |issue=6958 |pages=593–595 |pmid=14534579 |arxiv=astro-ph/0310253 |bibcode=2003Natur.425..593L |s2cid=4380713 }}</ref>

|bibcode=2010JCAP...07..003P |s2cid=118452299 }}</ref>), as well as on the theory of perturbations in non-isotropic space-times (of the type [[Bianchi classification|Bianchi I]]).<ref>{{cite |first3=Jean-Philippe |journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics |volume=2007 |issue=9 |page=006 |arxiv=0707.0736 |bibcode=2007JCAP...09..006P |s2cid=119143078 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.78.063526 |title=Cosmic microwave background bispectrum on small angular scales |year=2008 |last1=Pitrou |first1=Cyril |last2=Uzan |first2=Jean-Philippe |last3=Bernardeau Uzan, [http://iopscience.iop.org/1475-7516/2008/04/004 Predictions from an anisotropic inflationary era], [[Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics|JCAP]] 04, 004 (2008)</ref> With Lev Kofman and Francis Bernardeau, he proposed an extension of [[Inflation (cosmology)|inflation]] leading to a modulation of perturbations during the warming phase.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.70.083004 |title=Modulated fluctuations from hybrid inflation |year=2004 |last1=Bernardeau |first1=Francis |last2=Kofman |first2=Lev |last3=Uzan |first3=Jean-Philippe |journal=Physical Review D |volume=70 |issue=8 |article-number=083004 |arxiv=astro-ph/0403315 |bibcode=2004PhRvD..70h3004B |s2cid=119411642 |url=https://hal.science/hal-04111289 }}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
* 2010: [[Prix Paul-Langevin]] of the [[Société française de physique]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Prix Paul Langevin|website=Société Française de Physique (sfpnet.fr)|date=15 April 2025 |url=https://www.sfpnet.fr/prix/prix-paul-langevin}}</ref>
* 2011: Prix spécial du Festival d'astronomie de Haute-Maurienne, for the book ''Multivers – mondes possibles de l'astrophysique, de la philosophie et de l'imaginaire''.
* 2015: [[Prix Georges Lemaître]]
* 2016: The composer {{ill|Fabien Waksman|fr}} dedicated to Uzan the musical composition ''Le baiser de la mort'' (The kiss of death), a quintet for string quartet and piano. 
* 2016: The arboretum du Val des Dames<ref>{{cite web|title=Gretz-Armainvilliers: arboretum du Val des Dames|website=Coleur Jardin|url=http://www.77couleurjardin.com/pages/jardins-par-secteur/secteur-ouest/gretz-armainvilliers-arboretum-du-val-des-dames.html}}</ref> in [[Gretz-Armainvilliers]] honoured him on October 27, 2016, with the planting of a tree (''[[Populus lasiocarpa]]'').
* 2019: Prix Ciel et Espace du livre d'astronomie 2019, for the book ''Big-Bang - comprendre l'univers depuis ici et maintenant''
* 2020: The asteroid [[35391 Uzan]] (having a diameter of about 5&nbsp;km in diameter) is named in his honour.<ref>{{cite journal|title=(35391) Uzan = 1997 XN3 (entry on page 16)|journal=WGSBN Bulletin|volume=1|issue=1|publisher=Working Group Small Bodies Nomenclature, International Astronomical Union|url=https://www.iau.org/static/publications/wgsbn-bulletins/wgsbn-bulletin-2101.pdf|archive-date=2021-07-02|access-date=2023-06-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210702032908/https://www.iau.org/static/publications/wgsbn-bulletins/wgsbn-bulletin-2101.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2025: [[Prix Jules Janssen]] awarded by the [[Société astronomique de France]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prix Jules Janssen |url=https://saf-astronomie.fr/en-janssen-prize/}}</ref>
